**Short answer:** Pick a power bank rated 100 Wh or less. Anything up to about 27,000 mAh is generally fine. From the results I have, the Baseus Blade H1 is a good option, but it's the only specific model they cover, so I can't call it the best of all the options.

**The Baseus Blade H1 (20,000 mAh, 100 W), $89.99**
- It's about 74 Wh, so it's under the 100 Wh airline limit. The product page lists it as carry-on legal.
- The 100 W USB-C output can charge a laptop, and it has 2× USB-C and 2× USB-A ports.
- It has a digital display, pass-through charging, and a 100 W cable in the box.
- It's flat (134 × 134 × 18 mm) and weighs about 451 g, so it fits in a personal item.
- The warranty is 24 months, with a 7-day no-reason return.
- Buy it here: https://dealectric.com/baseus-blade-h1-100w-20000mah. The page's buy button opens Baseus's official US store. It's an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you. The price was verified on 2026-10-21 and may have changed, so check at checkout.

**Rules to know before you fly**
- Power banks go in your carry-on only, never checked bags. If your carry-on gets gate-checked, take the power bank out and keep it with you. ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries))
- The limit is 100 Wh per battery. With airline approval, you can bring up to two larger ones (101–160 Wh). Anything over 160 Wh is not allowed. ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7))
- To check the rating yourself, divide mAh by 1000 and multiply by the voltage. Most power banks use about 3.7 V, which is how 20,000 mAh comes out to about 74 Wh.
- Protect the terminals from short circuits, for example by leaving the bank in its packaging or covering the ports. Don't bring damaged or recalled batteries.
- Airlines can be stricter than the FAA. **Southwest** now limits each passenger to **one** power bank (effective April 20, 2026). It must be 100 Wh or less and can't go in the overhead bin. You can't charge it from in-seat power, and it must be visible while in use. ([Southwest](https://support.southwest.com/helpcenter/article/Traveling-with-lithium-batteries-e-cigarettes-and-lighters)) Check your own airline's policy before you go. If you're flying internationally, [IATA's guidance](https://www.iata.org/en/youandiata/travelers/batteries/) says rules vary by airline and country.

**Choosing one:** If you only need to top up a phone, a smaller 10,000 mAh bank (about 37 Wh) is lighter and cheaper. The Blade H1 makes sense if you want one bank for both a laptop and a phone. If you tell me your devices and airline, I can narrow it down.
